sectors.trend: Iron ore downside persists, pressuring major miners; however, gold exploration in WA/SA and rare earths (Dalaroo) show small/mid-cap resilience
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from weak iron ore; gold juniors (Platina, Broken Hill, Forrestania, Great Southern) offer speculative upside; Dalaroo rare earths play aligns with supply-chain diversification

sectors.trend: Hawkish RBA (Bullock) supports NIMs but housing stress and ASIC private credit warnings create credit risk; super contribution surge is a tailwind
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from rate environment but face housing-driven credit concerns; ASIC scrutiny of private credit (#14, #60) may tighten funding conditions

sectors.trend: Sydney housing 'bloodbath' and auction market reality check signal cooling; rental market disruption from agent-bypass models
sectors.implications: Property and healthcare REITs (e.g., GPT.AX, ICPS.AX) face cap-rate pressure; rental yield compression possible as agent fees are challenged

sectors.trend: Diesel and petrol prices rising, feeding inflation; EV adoption accelerating as consumers flee bowser
sectors.implications: Woodside.AX, Santos.AX benefit from firm energy prices; long-term EV transition pressures oil demand; inflation risk supports RBA hawkish stance

sectors.trend: NDIS funding gaps and coroner findings highlight systemic issues; no major ASX-listed healthcare catalysts today
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX remain defensive anchors; NDIS policy risk is a watch item for healthcare services

sectors.trend: Super contributions surge 33%+ post-budget; new government-backed digital pension scheme proposed as parallel to super
sectors.implications: Super fund managers (HUB.AX, PPA.AX) see AUM tailwind; digital pension scheme could disrupt long-term super model; ASIC private credit warnings affect fund allocations

Iron ore structural downside pressures ASX materials weight
Housing market correction in Sydney threatens bank credit and REIT valuations
Private credit sector under ASIC scrutiny – systemic financial stability risk
Gold and rare earths exploration activity in WA/SA supports small-cap miners
Geopolitical fragmentation (US trade war, China instability, EU political turmoil)
Energy price shock feeding inflation, complicating RBA path
Super/pension reform: contribution surge vs. new digital pension parallel system

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA sustained hawkish policy / higher-for-longer rates
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight financials (NIM benefit); underweight REITs and rate-sensitive growth; hedge with gold exposure

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Iron ore price decline pressuring ASX materials
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX weight; rotate into gold and rare earths juniors

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Private credit sector instability / ASIC intervention
risk_assessment.mitigation: Avoid leveraged credit exposures; monitor ASIC enforcement actions; favour listed equities over private credit funds

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Sydney housing market correction / credit deterioration
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor bank NPL data; reduce REIT exposure; favour defensive consumer staples (WES.AX, WOW.AX)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Geopolitical escalation (US trade war, China political risk)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Maintain diversified global exposure; hold AUD-hedged positions; monitor commodity demand from China
Overweight energy producers (WDS.AX, STO.AX); monitor CPI data for RBA reaction

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and rare earths explorers in WA/SA
opportunities.rationale: Active drilling results (10.72g/t Great Southern, Broken Hill sulphides, Dalaroo rare earths) signal discovery phase; gold hedges rate uncertainty

opportunities.recommendation: Maintain overweight in major banks for NIM support
opportunities.rationale: Hawkish RBA sustains NIMs; super contribution surge supports fee income; credit risk manageable if housing stabilises

opportunities.recommendation: Selective energy exposure on fuel price shock
opportunities.rationale: Rising diesel/petrol prices support upstream producers; EV transition is long-term but near-term demand firm

defensive_moves.rationale: Persistent iron ore downside threatens BHP, RIO, FMG earnings; China demand uncertainty elevated
Sydney housing bloodbath and rising rates pressure valuations; auction market cooling signals demand weakness

defensive_moves.recommendation: Avoid private credit and leveraged fund exposures
defensive_moves.rationale: ASIC warning and Odey collapse signal sector fragility; liquidity risk in stressed conditions

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hold defensive consumer staples as portfolio ballast
defensive_moves.rationale: Inflation shock and rate uncertainty favour essential-goods defensives

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound ('treading water') as RBA hawkish bias, iron ore weakness, and housing stress cap upside. Geopolitical noise (US trade war, China) adds volatility. Gold juniors and banks may outperform; materials and REITs lag. 1–3 month range: ^AXJO 8,200–8,600.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautious. Structural iron ore decline and China demand softness pressure materials. Housing correction may moderate by H2 2026 if RBA eases. Super/pension reform and rare earths/gold exploration offer structural themes. Geopolitical fragmentation is a persistent drag on global risk appetite.

CBA.AX, NAB.AX NIM and credit metrics
China PMI and property sector data
